total.description: Every client visible to the calling admin.

totalAmount.description: Monetary value — ALWAYS a string, never a number. NUMERIC(28,8) at rest; Number()/parseFloat on this field truncates past 2^53 (ARCHITECTURE §6.1).

byState.description: One entry per transaction_state, always all of them, covering withdrawals only (direction = withdrawal). Deposits are excluded.

applications.description: Application count per ib_application_status (pending, approved, rejected). All values always present.

partners.description: Rows in ib_accounts — partners on the books, active or not.

clients.description: Present only with users.view. ABSENT — not zeroed — otherwise.

kyc.description: Present only with kyc.view or kyc.review. ABSENT otherwise.

withdrawals.description: Present only with withdrawals.view. ABSENT otherwise.

ib.description: Present only with ib.view. ABSENT otherwise.

sections.description: The sections this response actually carries, so a screen reads a list rather than probing for undefined keys.

scoped.description: True when the calling admin is restricted to a subset of clients, in which case every number above counts only THEIR clients. A screen showing a headline total to a scoped admin without saying so invites it to be read as a platform total.

count.description: Registrations that day. 0 for a day with none — never omitted.

days.description: The window actually served, echoed back.

points.description: Exactly `days` entries, oldest first, one per calendar day with no gaps.

scoped.description: True when these counts cover only the actor’s own clients.

submitted.description: Submissions whose submitted_at falls on this day.

approved.description: Submissions REVIEWED on this day whose status is approved. A rejection reviewed the same day is not counted here.

totalAmount.description: Monetary value — ALWAYS a string, never a number (§6.1). "0" for a day with no withdrawals, never null.

points.description: Exactly `days` entries, no gaps. Bucketed on when the withdrawal was REQUESTED (created_at), which is the only date defined for a pending or rejected request.

balance.description: Monetary value — ALWAYS a string, never a number. NUMERIC(28,8) exceeds what a JavaScript number represents exactly, so Number()/parseFloat lose value before any formatting starts (§6.1).

onHold.description: Reserved against a pending transfer — a string for the same reason as `balance`. Available = balance − onHold, and that subtraction belongs in decimal arithmetic.

login.description: The MT5 login, once there is an MT5 to issue one. NULL until assigned, and a STRING rather than a number because leading zeros are significant to the bridge.

balance.description: Monetary value — ALWAYS a string. CRM-owned until the MT5 bridge lands, at which point it becomes a mirror of MT5 or is removed (see the schema comment).

statusCode.description: HTTP status, repeated in the body for convenience.

code.description: Machine-readable cause, from a closed set. BRANCH ON THIS, never on `message` — the message is prose, is localised, and is reworded without notice.

message.example: Please verify your email address before accessing this resource.
message.description: Human-readable and safe to display. Never parse it.

fields.description: Present only on validation failures: field path → what is wrong with it. Dotted for nested DTOs, so a form can attach each message to the input that caused it.

requestId.description: The correlation id for this request (R-6.1). Stamped on every log line the API wrote while handling it, so quoting it in a support ticket is enough to find them.

path.description: The path as served, with query values redacted.
